preconditions.expression: n == int(stdin.split()[0]) and len(s) == n and len(t) == n and all(c in '01' for c in s) and all(c in '01' for c in t)
preconditions.description: Input consists of a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^6) followed by two binary strings s and t of length n, each containing only '0' and '1'.

postconditions.description: Output is either -1 (impossible to convert s to t) or a non-negative integer representing the minimum number of operations required (0 ≤ N ≤ n).

postconditions.expression: (stdout == '-1') == any(s.count('1') != t.count('1'), any(s[i] != t[i] for i in range(n) if s[i] == '0' and t[i] == '1'))
postconditions.description: If the number of '1's in s and t differ or there exists a position i where s[i] is '0' and t[i] is '1', output is -1 (impossible).
If s is already equal to t, output is 0.

postconditions.expression: all(s[i] == t[i] or (s[i] == '1' and t[i] == '0') for i in range(n)) if stdout != '-1' else True
postconditions.description: If output is not -1, for every position i, either s[i] == t[i] or s[i] is '1' and t[i] is '0' (i.e., no '0' in s must become '1' in t).

postconditions.expression: int(stdout) == min(operations) if stdout != '-1' else True
postconditions.description: If output is not -1, it is the minimum number of operations required to convert s to t, where each operation is a rotation of a subsequence of s. The operations are defined as follows: a rotation of a subsequence of indices I is valid if rotating the bits at those indices clockwise once brings s closer to t. The minimum number of operations is the smallest k such that after k valid rotations, s equals t.
